text.en: A writer of the time said that the early British in Bengal treated land and people as fair game for plunder. How did traders become rulers?

Colonialism is the practice in which one country takes control of another region, sets up settlements there and imposes its political, economic and cultural systems.
From the 15th century European powers like Spain, Portugal, Britain, France and the Netherlands set up colonies in Africa, Asia and the Americas.
Europeans were drawn to India by trade in spices, textiles and wealth, and by the sea route found by Vasco da Gama in 1498.
The English East India Company, started in 1600, gained control by winning the Battle of Plassey in 1757 and the Battle of Buxar in 1764.
The Company used military power, treaties and taxes, and took over Indian kingdoms one by one.
In 1741 the Travancore ruler defeated the Dutch at Colachel, a rare victory over a European power.
The Company collected high land revenue, and Indian handloom textiles lost markets to cheap factory-made British cloth.
Indian wealth flowed to Britain, which many Indian thinkers called the drain of wealth.
After the revolt of 1857, the British Crown took over rule in 1858 and the British Raj began.
The colonial era also brought railways, English education and laws, but the main aim was British profit, not Indian welfare.

problem.en: How did the Company win control of Bengal?

text.en: It defeated the Nawab of Bengal at Plassey in 1757.
It won the Battle of Buxar in 1764.
It then collected the revenue of Bengal.

prompt.en: Why was colonialism harmful to India's economy?

requiredIdeas.en: Wealth was taken out of India.

points.en: Colonialism is control of one region by another country.
The Company won Plassey (1757) and Buxar (1764); Crown rule began in 1858.
The drain of wealth and loss of crafts hurt India.
